metadata.name: HAS-BLED Score for Major Bleeding Risk
metadata.summary: 9-point score identifying modifiable bleeding risk factors in patients on anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation.
clinical_pearls: A high HAS-BLED score (>= 3) is NOT a contraindication to anticoagulation; it flags patients needing closer monitoring and correction of modifiable risks (BP, NSAIDs, alcohol, labile INR).
Annual major bleeding rate increases progressively with higher HAS-BLED scores across both VKA- and DOAC-treated cohorts.
Pitfall — Overlapping stroke and bleeding factors: Many components of HAS-BLED (age, hypertension, prior stroke) also drive stroke risk and favor anticoagulation.

Pitfall — Limited accuracy in CKD and cancer: HAS-BLED performs poorly in end-stage kidney disease and active malignancy; newer tools (e.g., DOAC Score) may better predict bleeding on direct oral anticoagulants.
Pitfall — Guideline stance: Major US and European AF guidelines emphasize addressing modifiable bleeding risks rather than relying on any single bleeding score cutoff to withhold anticoagulation.

items.label: Abnormal Renal Function (dialysis, transplant, or SCr >= 200 µmol/L [2.26 mg/dL])
Abnormal Liver Function (cirrhosis, or bilirubin > 2x ULN with AST/ALT > 3x ULN)

interpretation.label: High Bleeding Risk (>= 3)
interpretation.summary: HAS-BLED >= 3: address modifiable bleeding risks and schedule closer follow-up; do not withhold indicated anticoagulation solely for high score.

assessment_guides.title: Labile INR Rule
bedside_steps: Apply only to patients currently taking a vitamin K antagonist (warfarin/acenocoumarol).
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Patients on DOACs or anticoagulation-naive patients score 0 for Labile INR.
